title: Parable of the ten virgins part 2
scripture_text: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went to meet the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish, and five were wise. The five who were foolish didn’t take enough olive oil for their lamps, but the other five were wise enough to take along extra oil. When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep. “At midnight they were roused by the shout, ‘Look, the bridegroom is coming! Come out and meet him!’ “All the bridesmaids got up and prepared their lamps. Then the five foolish ones asked the others, ‘Please give us some of your oil because our lamps are going out.’ “But the others replied, ‘We don’t have enough for all of us. Go to a shop and buy some for yourselves.’ “But while they were gone to buy oil, the bridegroom came. Then those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was locked. Later, when the other five bridesmaids returned, they stood outside, calling, ‘Lord! Lord! Open the door for us!’ “But he called back, ‘Believe me, I don’t know you!’ “So you, too, must keep watch! For you do not know the day or hour of my return.’’
devotional:
Understanding the Parable.

To help us learn something from the parable let us ask this question. The five foolish bridesmaids brought no oil. What does that say about them and what was going on in their hearts and minds?

The fact that the five foolish bridesmaids had no oil was an expression of their mindset, of their world view; it was a consequence of how they had always looked at life and the world around them. Coming to the feast without oil was an ongoing natural expression of how they had always lived. So in this parable Jesus is warning us, if you think like these foolish bridesmaids, you may share their fate. If we have the same mindset as them then we will not be ready for Jesus’ return as they were not ready for the bridegroom. So what has this to teach us?

They refused to engage their minds and think things through. When Jesus refers to the five wise bridesmaids he does not use the usual word for wisdom which is Sophia, rather he uses the word ‘phronimos could be better translated as "thoughtful" or "considerate" (in the sense of someone who tries to consider all the facts in order to make a wise judgment.) Often as Christians we seldom take the time to sit down and think through what we believe, why we believe it and what the consequences of our beliefs are. We come to church, we sit in our pews and often we are disengaged from what is being said. Jesus would have never taught the way we teach today. In Jesus’ day, during the teaching, there was always some kind of interaction, between him and those he was teaching. A lot of our lethargy is rooted in our thinking. Our English word for lethargic comes from the Greek word lethargos which means forgetfulness. So it is very important that we use our minds that we ask questions, that we wrestle with scriptures, and work hard to get a better understanding of what they are saying.

These foolish virgins were half hearted in how they lived. How do we know that? Well the text tells us that they brought their lamps but no oil; think about that, it doesn’t make sense; it’s like us buying a lamp and not buying a bulb to put in it. They approached their role as bridesmaids with a half hearted attitude.

Being half-hearted about our relationship with Jesus will likely prevent us from finishing the race, we will give up. The nature of Christianity is such that it requires us to be passionate about it. A Christian without passion is like paint without colour, or music without sound. It doesn’t make any sense.

C.S. Lewis said, ‘Our Lord finds our desires not too strong, but too weak. We are half-hearted creatures, fooling about with drink and sex and ambition, when infinite joy is offered to us, like an ignorant child who wants to go on making mud pies in the slum because he cannot imagine what is meant by the offer of a holiday at the sea. We are far too easily pleased.’ C.S.Lewis: - The Weight of Glory, and Other Addresses

For these foolish bridesmaids, looking right was more important than being right. As you read this story you will notice that there was no mention of any external differences between the wise and foolish bridesmaids. They all looked as if they were honestly fulfilling their role, until the lack of oil of the foolish bridesmaids is mentioned. They looked the part to the onlooker, but in reality reputation was more important than authenticity. The life of a child of God in the kingdom should be one of authenticity, we should never appear to be one thing and in reality be something completely different.
prayer: Father Am I a Christian without passion like paint without colour?
